segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme …pe…
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. …
“Mendicants, I will teach you about the gods of the centaur realm.
And what are the gods of the centaur realm?
There are gods who live in fragrant roots,
These are called the gods of the centaur realm.”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, that mendicant said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā gandhabbakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why someone, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the company of the gods of the centaur realm?”

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena sucaritaṁ carati, vācāya sucaritaṁ carati, manasā sucaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: “Mendicant, it’s when someone does good things by way of body, speech, and mind.
‘The gods of the centaur realm are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

segs.p: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā gandhabbakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
segs.e: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods of the centaur realm!’

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā gandhabbakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the centaur realm.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā gandhabbakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī”ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why someone, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the company of the gods of the centaur realm.”

segs.e: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why someone, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the company of the gods who live in fragrant roots?”

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena sucaritaṁ carati, vācāya sucaritaṁ carati, manasā sucaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: “Mendicant, it’s when someone does good things by way of body, speech, and mind.
‘The gods who live in fragrant roots are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

segs.p: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā mūlagandhe adhivatthānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
segs.e: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods who live in fragrant roots!’
They give gifts of fragrant roots.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā mūlagandhe adhivatthānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods who live in fragrant roots.
This is the cause, this is the reason why someone, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the company of the gods who live in fragrant roots.”

segs.p: yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā mūlagandhe adhivatthānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī”ti.

segs.e: Nine Discourses On Givers of Fragrant Heartwood, Etc.
